Austine Muharia

Founder & Owner, Peanut Butter Bliss

Austine started Peanut Butter Bliss with a simple belief: good food should be honest. Frustrated by spreads packed with additives, he began roasting and grinding peanuts in his own kitchen, tweaking every batch until the taste was right.

Friends and family kept coming back for more jars. What began as a kitchen experiment grew into a brand built on pure peanuts, careful craft and the comfort of a spoonful of something real.

Today Austine still oversees every batch personally. His promise to every home is the same: rich flavour, smooth texture and nutrition you can trust.

Featured · Health & Nutrition

Health Benefits of Peanut Butter: Creamy vs Crunchy

Peanut butter is more than a tasty spread. Both creamy (smooth) and crunchy peanut butter can provide valuable nutrients that support energy, muscle health, heart health and overall well-being.

The main difference is texture: creamy peanut butter has finely ground peanuts, while crunchy peanut butter contains small pieces of peanuts. If both are made from the same ingredients, their nutritional benefits are very similar.

1. Major health benefits of peanut butter

1. Provides energy for daily activities

Peanuts contain healthy fats, protein and carbohydrates. These nutrients provide energy for walking, working, studying, exercising and other everyday activities. Peanut butter is especially useful when you need a filling snack between meals.

2. Supports muscle growth and repair

Peanut butter provides plant-based protein, which supplies amino acids needed to build and repair body tissues. It can complement other protein sources such as eggs, beans, milk, yoghurt, fish and meat.

3. Supports heart health

Much of the fat in peanuts is unsaturated fat, including monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats. Replacing some saturated fats with unsaturated fats can help improve blood cholesterol levels and support cardiovascular health.

4. Helps you feel satisfied for longer

The combination of protein, fat and some fibre can help you feel full after eating. Adding peanut butter to breakfast or a snack may help you stay satisfied between meals.

5. Supplies important vitamins and minerals

Peanut butter contains vitamin E, magnesium, phosphorus, niacin (vitamin B3) and manganese. These nutrients help support normal body functions, including energy metabolism, nerve function and protection of cells from oxidative damage.

6. Supports normal digestive health

Peanuts contain dietary fibre, which contributes to normal bowel function. Peanut butter contains some fibre, although whole peanuts and other fibre-rich foods such as beans, vegetables, fruits and whole grains are also important for digestive health.

7. Supports healthy weight management

Because peanut butter is filling and energy-dense, a suitable portion can help provide lasting satisfaction as part of balanced meals. It can fit into different nutritional goals, but eating more than your body needs can add substantial energy to your diet.

8. Provides antioxidants

Peanuts contain compounds such as vitamin E and polyphenols that help protect cells against oxidative damage. Peanut butter retains some of these compounds, although the amount depends on processing and ingredients.

2. Creamy vs crunchy: which is healthier?

Creamy peanut butter

  • Easy to spread on bread and chapati.
  • Blends smoothly into porridge, milkshakes and smoothies.
  • Provides protein, healthy fats and essential minerals.
  • Useful for adding nutrients to soft foods.

Crunchy peanut butter

  • Provides similar protein, fats, vitamins and minerals.
  • Offers a satisfying crunch and more texture.
  • May contain slightly different amounts of fibre or other nutrients depending on how it is made.
  • Works well on toast, sandwiches and as a topping for oats.

Our take: neither type is automatically healthier. Choose based on your preference and compare the ingredient lists and nutrition labels. A product made mainly from peanuts, with little or no added sugar and moderate sodium, is generally a good choice.

3. What nutrients do you get from peanut butter?

A typical two-tablespoon serving (about 32 g) provides approximately the following. Exact values vary by brand and recipe.

NutrientApproximate amountWhy it matters
Energy180–200 caloriesFuels daily activities
Protein7–8 gBuilds and repairs body tissues
Total fat15–17 gProvides energy and helps absorb vitamins
Fibre1.5–3 gSupports normal digestion
Vitamin EVariesHelps protect cells
MagnesiumVariesSupports muscles and nerves
Niacin (B3)VariesHelps the body release energy from food
PhosphorusVariesSupports bones and normal cell function

These are approximate nutritional values, not a guarantee for every product.

4. What is the best way to eat peanut butter?

With whole-grain bread

Combines protein and healthy fats with carbohydrates and fibre for a satisfying breakfast or snack.

With porridge

Adds flavour, protein and healthy fats to oats or porridge made from other grains.

In a smoothie

Blend peanut butter with banana and milk or a fortified alternative for a nourishing drink.

With fruit

Pair it with apples or bananas for a convenient snack with a mix of nutrients.

5. Important things to know

Peanut allergies

Peanuts can cause serious allergic reactions. Anyone with a peanut allergy should avoid peanut butter.

Added sugar

Some commercial products contain added sugar. Check the label, especially if you want a less sweet product.

Added salt

Compare sodium levels if you want to limit salt in your diet.

Portion size

Peanut butter is nutritious but energy-dense. Enjoy it as part of balanced meals and snacks rather than as your only source of nutrition.

Food safety

Store it according to the label and keep it protected from moisture and contamination.

Peanut butter is not a medicine, and it does not by itself prevent or cure diseases. Its benefits come from being part of an overall balanced diet.

More from the blog

Honey Peanut Butter: the golden twist on a classic

Honey Peanut Butter takes our handcrafted peanut butter and pairs it with natural honey. You get the rich, roasted flavour of real peanuts, rounded off with a gentle golden sweetness. It is the jar for people who want a little something extra on the spoon.

Why peanuts and honey work so well together
Peanuts are savoury, toasty and rich. Honey is sweet, floral and bright. Together they balance each other, so the spread tastes full without needing anything else added to it.

Ways to enjoy it

• Breakfast toast: spread it on warm bread or chapati and add banana slices.
• Porridge and oats: stir a spoonful into hot porridge for natural sweetness and creaminess.
• Pancakes and waffles: warm it slightly and drizzle it over the top instead of syrup.
• Smoothies: blend with banana, milk and ice for a filling drink.
• Snack time: pair it with apple slices, crackers or celery sticks.
• Straight from the spoon: no recipe needed.

Quick recipe: honey peanut energy bites
Mix 4 tablespoons of Honey Peanut Butter with 1 cup of rolled oats and a handful of raisins or chopped dates. Roll into small balls and chill for 30 minutes. They make an easy snack for school, work or after a workout.

Sizes and prices
250g KSH 200, 500g KSH 400, 1kg KSH 700 and 1.5kg KSH 1200. Pick 250g to try it, or a larger jar if the whole family is hooked.

Storage tips
Keep the jar tightly closed in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Natural oil can rise to the top, so give it a stir before using. Use a clean, dry spoon each time.

Meet Pure Nut Oil: golden oil from real peanuts

Our Pure Nut Oil is extracted from carefully selected peanuts and made at home in small batches, with no additives and no preservatives. The result is a clear golden oil with a light, nutty aroma.

Where it shines in the kitchen
Use it to fry chapati, potatoes and fish, to sauté vegetables, or to roast and stir-fry. It handles heat well, so it suits everyday Kenyan cooking from breakfast to supper.

Choosing your jar
Start with 250g (KSH 200) to try it, take 500g (KSH 350) for a regular household, or go for 1kg (KSH 500) if you cook daily or for a big family.

Keeping it fresh
Store the jar tightly closed in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight, and use a clean, dry spoon or pour straight from the jar.

5 ways to eat peanut butter before 9am

Stir it into oats, swirl it over banana toast, blend it into a smoothie, spread it on pancakes, or pair it with apple slices. Each gives lasting energy.

Smooth, creamy or crunchy: which one are you?

Smooth suits sandwiches and sauces. Creamy is for spooning. Crunchy adds texture to toast and snack bowls. Honey adds a touch of golden sweetness.

Why peanut butter is a protein-rich staple

Peanuts are a source of protein, healthy fats and fibre. Choosing a jar made from real peanuts with no unnecessary extras keeps it wholesome.

Peanut butter banana smoothie in 2 minutes

Blend one banana, a big spoon of peanut butter, a cup of milk and a few ice cubes. Sweeten with honey if you like.

What makes a handcrafted jar different

Small batches let us watch the roast, the grind and the texture. That attention is what you taste.

Storing your jar

Keep it sealed and cool. Natural oil may rise to the top, so stir before use.
